description: Operationalize the Luminumbra polyglot-audit final roadmap's must-fix block: lock the SHIELD contract (Stage 0), make the build trustworthy (Stage 1), fix concurrency + chunk ownership (Stage 2), and unify runtime logging (Stage 3.1). Optional stages (S3.2+, S4-S8) are deferred to a follow-on dispatch once the must-fix block lands.

tasks.title: Add CPU/GPU SDF parity test harness (initially skipped)
tasks.prompt: Add a parity-test harness that compares CPU SDF generation (SHIELD_WorldSystem::GenerateChunkData) to GPU SDF generation (the compute shader path invoked via SHIELD_WorldSystem::m_gpu_sdf_callback / RenderPipeline::generate_chunk_sdf_gpu). The test fixture must enumerate three known seeds and three chunk coordinates, generate SDFs both ways, and assert per-cell agreement within 1e-5 absolute tolerance. Because the GPU path requires an OpenGL context, mark each test case GTEST_SKIP() with a TODO referencing T-S0-6 if no GL context is available; the harness must compile and run cleanly in the existing test binary. Register the new test source in test/CMakeLists.txt. Verify with cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure (the skipped tests should report SKIPPED, not FAILED). Do NOT modify any production source in this task.

tasks.title: Flip SDF sign convention to inside-negative across CPU + GPU paths
tasks.prompt: Adopt inside-negative as the SDF sign convention. (1) In SHIELD_WorldSystem::get_density_at_from_precalculated() (around line 279), change terrain_density = terrain_height - world_pos.y to terrain_density = world_pos.y - terrain_height. (2) Mirror the change in SHIELD_WorldSystem::GenerateChunkData() at the SDF write (around lines 420 and 440). (3) Flip the GPU-path post-generation surface-detection loop in SHIELD_WorldSystem::GenerateChunkData() at line 354: change if (chunk.sdf_data[sdf_idx] > 0.0f) to if (chunk.sdf_data[sdf_idx] < 0.0f) so the heightmap reconstruction from GPU SDF still finds the surface under the new sign convention. (4) Audit every other consumer of chunk.sdf_data inside SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp via Grep — any direct comparison with a literal must be reviewed for sign-direction; document each in the commit message. (5) Audit the GPU compute shader res/shaders/sdf_generation.compute (and any other *.compute file that writes terrain SDF) and apply the same sign flip there. (6) After the change, the SurfaceIsGeneratedAtCorrectHeight test must pass: inside_density < 0 (point at y=4 with terrain_height=8), outside_density > 0 (point at y=12 with terrain_height=8). Do NOT modify MarchingCubes.cpp in this task — that comparison (val < isolevel) is already correct under inside-negative. Do NOT modify any test source in this task. Verify with cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --gtest_filter=*SurfaceIsGeneratedAtCorrectHeight*.

tasks.title: Verify and fix mesh normal winding after sign flip
tasks.prompt: After T-S0-1, run ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --gtest_filter=*NormalsPointUpwardsOnHorizontalSurface*. If it passes, stop — there is no work to do. If it fails (normals point down): the embedded MarchingCubesTables.inl may have been authored against inside-positive. Inspect the table-consumption loop at MarchingCubes.cpp:164 (the triTable winding) and the face-normal accumulation at lines 175-185. Apply the minimum change: either swap two indices in the triangle push (e.g., swap vert_indices[i+1] and vert_indices[i+2]) OR negate face_normal before accumulation. Pick whichever isolates the change to a single contiguous block. Document the choice with a one-line comment that names the convention. Verify by running --gtest_filter=*Normals*. Do not modify the SHIELD_WorldSystem or test source.

tasks.title: Fix or redefine cave-carving so caves change generated mesh
tasks.prompt: After the sign flip, audit whether cave_density = cave_carve_value * (cave_val - cave_threshold) still produces values that cross the isolevel (0.0) where the CavesChangeGeneratedMesh test expects them to. Under inside-negative convention, caves should INCREASE the SDF value at carved points so air bubbles appear inside terrain. The current formula adds a positive offset to terrain_density via std::min — under inside-negative this is the wrong direction. There are TWO call sites that both apply the cave term and must be edited consistently: (a) get_density_at_from_precalculated() at SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:287, and (b) GenerateChunkData() CPU fallback path at SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp:430. Replace std::min(terrain_density, cave_density) with std::max(terrain_density, -cave_density) (or equivalently invert cave_density's sign), so caves push the SDF upward through zero in solid regions. If the test still passes with different vertex counts but with values that disagree with the new physical meaning, update the test's cave_threshold/cave_frequency parameters to ensure measurable mesh divergence. The test's intent — verify cave generation has an observable effect on geometry — must be preserved; the exact numeric thresholds may be tuned. Verify with --gtest_filter=*CavesChange*. Do not modify MarchingCubes or other test files.

tasks.title: Write docs/shield/sdf-contract.md and link from README
tasks.prompt: Write docs/shield/sdf-contract.md as the single source of truth for SHIELD terrain semantics. Sections: (1) SDF sign convention (inside-negative, outside-positive). (2) Isolevel: 0.0. (3) SDF grid layout in Chunk::sdf_data (x varies fastest, then y, then z; padded by +1 in each dimension for MC neighborhood). (4) Terrain height contract (GetTerrainHeightAt returns world-space Y at a given x,z; clamped by island_mask if enabled). (5) Cave carve formula and valid threshold ranges (cite the post-T-S0-3 implementation). (6) Marching Cubes step semantics: ChunkLOD.step is the stride between sampled cells; meshing iterates by step, never by 1, for non-LOD-0 chunks. (7) Mesh normal direction (+Y on horizontal surfaces). Add a one-line note: 'If you change any value in this document, every consumer of SDF/mesh data must be re-validated.' Add a link from README.md (in a 'Documentation' or 'Architecture' section) pointing to docs/shield/sdf-contract.md. Do not modify any code.

tasks.title: Add LOD-step-aware mesh winding regression test
tasks.prompt: Add a regression test MeshNormalWindingIsConsistentUnderLodStep to test/shield/test_world_generation.cpp. The test: (1) Generates a flat-surface chunk using params_guaranteed_surface. (2) Polygonises it three times with step=1, step=2, step=4. (3) Asserts that every triangle in each mesh has the same winding direction by computing cross(v2-v1, v3-v1).y > 0 (consistent upward face normals). (4) Asserts that the three meshes have decreasing vertex counts (step=4 < step=2 < step=1). Do not modify production source; this is a test-only change. Verify with ctest --gtest_filter=*MeshNormalWinding*.

tasks.title: Enable the CPU/GPU SDF parity test in CI
tasks.prompt: Remove the GTEST_SKIP() guards from the parity test added in T-S0-0. To make GPU SDF reachable from the test binary, the test target must link GLFW + GLAD (today it only links luminumbra_common + gtest_main). Update test/CMakeLists.txt to add target_link_libraries(world_generation_test PRIVATE glfw glad) (and on Linux, opengl32/GL system libs as needed — match what luminumbra_client_app pulls). In the test, create a minimal headless OpenGL context using GLFW (glfwInit, glfwWindowHint(GLFW_VISIBLE, false), glfwWindowHint context-version 4.5, create a 1x1 hidden window, gladLoadGLLoader) within a SetUp/TearDown pair. The parity test invokes RenderPipeline::generate_chunk_sdf_gpu directly (or the m_gpu_sdf_callback indirection) and compares the resulting std::vector<float> to SHIELD_WorldSystem::GenerateChunkData()'s CPU output element-wise with 1e-5 tolerance. If glfwInit fails (CI machine without GL), the test logs a warning and SKIPs instead of failing — but a deliberate parity violation must FAIL. Verify with ctest --gtest_filter=*SdfParity*.

tasks.title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow (build + test + lint)
tasks.prompt: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml. Triggers: push to main and pull_request. Matrix: os in [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]. Steps per job: (1) checkout with submodules: recursive; (2) setup ninja on Linux, no extra setup on Windows (VS 2022 is preinstalled); (3) cache the vendor build via actions/cache keyed on hashFiles('vendor/**/CMakeLists.txt'); (4) cmake --preset release; (5) cmake --build --preset release; (6) ctest --preset release --output-on-failure; (7) bash scripts/lint.sh on Linux, pwsh scripts/lint.ps1 on Windows; (8) cargo install/run forge if available, then forge verify --validation-policy fail --testing-policy fail (allow this step to be a no-op via continue-on-error: true if forge is not installed in CI yet — we add it later). Workflow file must be <60 lines and use no third-party actions beyond actions/checkout@v4 and actions/cache@v4.

tasks.title: Replace JobSystem counter ring with per-handle owned atomics
tasks.prompt: Replace JobSystem's 256-slot ring of atomic counters with per-handle owned counters. Change struct JobHandle { std::atomic<int>* counter = nullptr; } to struct JobHandle { std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<int>> counter; }. Remove the m_counters std::array and m_next_counter_index fields. In dispatch_batch, allocate a fresh std::make_shared<std::atomic<int>>((int)jobs.size()) per call; each job lambda captures the shared_ptr by value (so the counter outlives the workers if necessary). wait() reads .load() through the shared_ptr. JobHandle consumers in src/ are: main_client.cpp (g_world_gen_handle), WaterSystem.cpp (water-sim batches), SHIELD_WorldSystem.cpp (generation + meshing). Audit each — they likely already store JobHandle by value (the previous struct's raw-pointer was a member, not the storage class), but verify and fix any that stored a JobHandle*. SHIELD_WorldSystem::dispatch_generation_jobs and dispatch_meshing_jobs must still return JobHandles by value — the caller decides what to keep. Add a comment over the new struct explaining the lifetime model. Verify with cmake --build --preset debug && ctest --preset debug --output-on-failure.

tasks.title: JobSystem::shutdown drains the queue and rejects new dispatch
tasks.prompt: Make JobSystem::shutdown drain the queue. Sequence: (1) Acquire m_queue_mutex; set m_stop_threads.store(true); release the lock. (2) Notify all workers. (3) Workers continue to pop and run jobs until the queue is empty AND m_stop_threads is true. (4) Wait for all workers to exit via join. (5) Pending JobHandles will see their shared counter drop to zero naturally as jobs complete (or stay non-zero forever if the queue was non-empty at start of shutdown — that's the caller's problem, not the JobSystem's). After shutdown, JobSystem::dispatch and dispatch_batch log an error and return a default-constructed JobHandle without queuing. Verify with cmake --build --preset debug && ctest. Add a doc comment explaining the drain-then-stop contract.

tasks.title: Introduce WorldStreamingState type + ChunkRenderable + atomic mesh publish on Chunk
tasks.prompt: Introduce only the new TYPES in this task; do not migrate any existing system. (1) Create world/WorldStreamingState.{h,cpp}: owns std::unordered_map<ChunkID, std::shared_ptr<Chunk>> guarded by std::shared_mutex, plus a Snapshot type that is std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const ChunkRenderable>>. Provide insert(id, chunk), erase(id), find(id) under unique_lock; provide snapshot() returning a Snapshot built under shared_lock. (2) Define ChunkRenderable as an immutable struct: ChunkID id, IVec3 coords, int current_lod, u32 mesh_version, std::shared_ptr<const MeshBuffers> terrain_mesh, std::shared_ptr<const MeshBuffers> water_mesh. (3) Add MeshBuffers as a struct holding std::vector<VoxelVertex> vertices, std::vector<u32> indices; place it in Chunk.h or a new MeshBuffers.h. (4) Modify Chunk to hold std::shared_ptr<const MeshBuffers> m_terrain_mesh and m_water_mesh as the publishable mesh; add Chunk::publish_terrain_mesh(std::shared_ptr<const MeshBuffers>) and publish_water_mesh that swap atomically (use std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<...>> if compiler supports C++20 atomic shared_ptr, else guard with a small std::mutex). (5) Keep the existing public std::vector mesh_vertices/mesh_indices/water_mesh_vertices/water_mesh_indices intact in this task — they remain the legacy write target during generation; the migration to read-via-snapshot happens in T-S2-4c. Add doc comments on the new APIs naming the lifetime + thread-safety contract. Verify with cmake --build --preset debug — no behavioral change yet.

tasks.title: Migrate SHIELD_WorldSystem to use WorldStreamingState and publish meshes

tasks.title: Add JobSystem and WorldStreamingState stress tests
tasks.prompt: Add stress tests. JobSystem_test.cpp: (1) DispatchOneThousandBatchesIntermixedWaits — dispatch 1000 batches of 10 jobs each, intermix wait() calls on alternating handles, assert every handle's counter reaches 0 exactly once; (2) ShutdownDrainsPendingJobs — queue 100 long jobs, call shutdown, assert all 100 finish before shutdown returns; (3) DispatchAfterShutdownReturnsInvalidHandle — call shutdown then dispatch, assert returned JobHandle is default-constructed. tasks.title: Embed git SHA + dirty flag as ENGINE_VERSION via CMake configure_file
tasks.prompt: Owner decision recorded: engine_version = git short SHA + dirty flag (e.g. '3f1af0b-dirty'). Implementation: (1) cmake/engine_version.cmake runs execute_process(COMMAND git rev-parse --short HEAD) and execute_process(COMMAND git diff --quiet -- :^.forge :^build :^data RESULT_VARIABLE GIT_DIRTY) to compute LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_VERSION_STRING and LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_GIT_DIRTY. Sets fallback 'unknown' if git is unavailable. (2) include(cmake/engine_version.cmake) from top-level CMakeLists.txt before add_subdirectory(src). (3) configure_file generates EngineVersion.h from EngineVersion.h.in into ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated/luminumbra/core/EngineVersion.h with #define LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_VERSION '@LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_VERSION_STRING@' and LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_VERSION_DIRTY @LUMINUMBRA_ENGINE_GIT_DIRTY@. (4) Add ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated as an include dir on luminumbra_common. (5) EngineVersion.cpp exposes free function const char* Luminumbra::engine_version() returning the macro. This API is consumed by WorldManifestV1 in T-S3-2 (out of scope here) to populate the manifest's engine_version field. Verify with cmake --preset debug && cmake --build --preset debug; grep the build dir for the generated header.

tasks.title: Replace WaterSystem first-transform hack with PlayerHandle lookup
tasks.prompt: WaterSystem.cpp:36-37 picks transform_view.front() as the camera position with a TODO 'Add proper camera/player tagging system'. Fix: (1) Add a tag component PlayerTag (empty struct) to components/CoreComponents.h. (2) PlayerController on construction emplaces the PlayerTag onto the player entity. (3) WaterSystem::update finds the player via auto player_view = registry.view<const TransformComponent, const PlayerTag>(); if exactly one match, use its transform; if zero or multiple, log a warning and fall back to Vec3(0). Remove the TODO. Verify with cmake --build --preset debug-asan && ctest --preset debug-asan.

tasks.title: Add round-trip test for asset_processor .lmesh format
tasks.prompt: Add a GoogleTest binary asset_processor_test under test/tools/. It (1) constructs a tiny in-memory .glb (or uses a single small fixture .glb under test/tools/fixtures/), (2) invokes asset_processor's core function — refactor asset_processor.cpp if needed to extract its meshopt + lmesh-writing pipeline into a callable function rather than only a main() — to produce a .lmesh in a temp directory, (3) loads the result via MeshLoader::Load, (4) asserts vertex count and index count are reasonable (>0) and the LMeshHeader's magic + counts match what was written. Register the new binary in test/CMakeLists.txt with gtest_discover_tests. Verify with ctest --preset debug --output-on-failure --gtest_filter=*AssetProcessor*.

tasks.title: Make LUMINUMBRA_ASSERT log+abort in Release, not no-op
tasks.prompt: Read core/Debug.h. If LUMINUMBRA_ASSERT(x, msg) is the standard 'do nothing in Release' assert(x) wrapper, change it: in Release, on failure, log msg via LUMINUMBRA_CORE_ERROR and call std::abort() (or std::quick_exit). In Debug, retain assert-style trap. The rationale (per quality-risks panel C2): startup paths like main_client.cpp use LUMINUMBRA_ASSERT(window, ...) — a null window in Release with the current macro silently dereferences. Add a doc comment explaining the Release-vs-Debug behavior. Do NOT change any call site of LUMINUMBRA_ASSERT. Verify with cmake --build --preset release && cmake --build --preset debug; both must compile.

tasks.title: Remove dead nested namespace declaration in GameSession.h
tasks.prompt: GameSession.h:27 contains a forward declaration of namespace Luminumbra::Systems INSIDE namespace Luminumbra::world, which creates the dead nested namespace Luminumbra::world::Luminumbra::Systems. Either (a) move the forward declaration outside the world:: namespace into the proper scope, or (b) delete the broken declaration entirely if GameSession.h already includes a concrete header that brings the real Luminumbra::Systems names into scope. Pick whichever yields the smaller diff. Verify GameSession.cpp still compiles with cmake --build --preset debug.
